intro: Two armies of sixteen pieces on a board of 64 squares. Play a friend on the same screen, or take on the computer at three strengths.
inspiredBy: Chess has been played for about 1,500 years. This is the standard game, with the standard rules.
goal: Checkmate the other king: attack it so that it has no way out. If a player has no legal move but isn't in check, it's a stalemate, and a draw.
howToPlay: Join with your phone. On your own, you play the computer; with two phones, you play each other.
In the lobby, choose your opponent, the computer's strength, your colour and a clock, then press {bolt} to start. White moves first.
On your turn, move your square with the arrows, then press {bolt} to pick up a piece. Dots show where it can go.
Move to one of those squares and press {bolt} to put it down. {drop} puts the piece back.
When a pawn reaches the far side, choose what it becomes with ◀▶ and press {bolt}. Usually a Queen.
To castle, pick up the King and move it two squares towards the Rook.
Press pause (❚❚) to offer a draw, resign, or leave. Your opponent accepts a draw with {bolt}.
steering: Move your square around the board
tips: Get your Knights and Bishops out early, and castle to keep your King safe.
Before every move, check what your opponent's last move attacks.
A piece that's attacked more times than it's defended can usually be taken.
The game is also a draw after three repeats of a position, or fifty moves each with no capture and no pawn moved.
Easy makes mistakes on purpose. Hard looks four moves ahead: watch out.
